reasons.realCost: The real bills at all three sizes land exactly on the plan sticker price -- $25, $39 and $39/mo -- because every current plan includes unlimited bandwidth and up to 1,000 pages.
reasons.pricingHonesty: Plan prices and per-plan transaction fees are published on the pricing page, though its 'save up to 36%' banner overstates the annual discount, which the plan prices themselves put at 24 to 28% depending on plan.
reasons.smallTeamFit: The drag-and-drop editor bundles a store, invoicing, scheduling and email marketing so a non-technical owner can run the site without a developer.
reasons.doesTheJob: One flat per-site subscription covers a website, blog/CMS, online store, invoicing, scheduling and email marketing, replacing several separate subscriptions.
reasons.freedomToLeave: Any plan can be canceled at any time and content exported via a WordPress XML file, though Squarespace warns some design elements and third-party links don't export and may delete site data 30 days after cancellation.
reasons.trackRecord: Squarespace has operated since 2003 and grandfathers legacy customers onto their original plan and fee terms rather than forcing them onto new pricing.

basis: Squarespace is the most predictable of the four: every real bill matches the sticker price, the bundled tools cover most of what a small owner needs, and the company has a long, stable public track record.
method: Two independent blind passes scored six factors (1–5) and an overall; published overall is the lower of the two overall scores, because this tool runs an affiliate program we have joined or may join. Pass scores: 4.3 and 4.1. Until we applied to Squarespace’s affiliate program on 27 September 2026, the published score was 4.2, the average of the two.
